h1: Quote Guide for Playground Equipment: What to Consider Before Purchasing

props.title: Quote Guide for Playground Equipment: What to Consider Before Purchasing
props.summaryText: What to send a supplier so the quote is accurate, what a complete playground quote should include, and how to compare two quotes that look nothing alike.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Wooden play deck with rope bridges over a blue patterned rubber surface

takeaways.text: The more you tell the supplier up front (site, users, budget), the more accurate and comparable the quote.
A complete quote lists every model, its specification, surfacing, civil work, transport, installation, warranty and GST.
The cheapest quote often leaves out surfacing, installation or taxes.
Put all quotes in one comparison table before you decide.

faq.q: How do I get a quote for playground equipment?
faq.a: Send the supplier your site dimensions and photos, the type of ground, the ages and number of children, any theme or equipment you have in mind, your timeline and a budget range. Ask for a layout drawing and a line-by-line quote.

faq.q: What should a playground equipment quote include?
faq.a: Each item with its model, size and specification; safety surfacing with type, thickness and area; civil and base work; transport; installation; warranty terms; GST; and the delivery and installation timeline.

faq.q: Why do playground quotes vary so much?
faq.a: Quotes often cover different scopes and materials. One may include surfacing, installation and GST while another does not, or use thinner steel and plastic. Compare quotes line by line on the same scope.
